Markup over time-to-event, capped against monitored
Resale asks as markup over face value, placed on the simulated horizon: the further right a point sits, the
closer the event. One series per mode.
run sw20261108T054830Z6297 | event evt_capped | mode capped | 51 rows | sha256 d8fbe6a50b4efbf2..
run sw20261108T054830Z6297 | event evt_monitored | mode monitored | 55 rows | sha256 92dba3b4261937f3..
DRY RUN: a simulated gateway returned what the hook would have done. No transaction was built, signed or
simulated rounds left to the event: 12 on the left, 0 (event day) on the right
markers are single resale attempts: filled = executed, x = refused by the cap, hollow = an ask nobody met. The short
rule is the median executed markup at that point on the horizon, labelled with the number of executed resales it was
taken over; a dashed segment joins two neighbouring points only when both have n >= 2, because a median of one trade
is a price and not a trend. On this chart 0 neighbouring pair(s) have n >= 2 on both ends.
No two neighbouring points have two observations each, so no median line is drawn: joining single trades would read as
a markup trend over the run.
The two modes differ in one thing only: the cap_bps written into the record. Monitored is the same predicate at the
field maximum, so nothing scripted can price above it.
Markup is integer arithmetic from price and face, the same value the dataset carries and its verifier re-checks.
